hypothesis: Can leakage-safe pre-origin diagnostics identify B3 failure risk and a repairable mechanism?
validation_contract: Origins 2011-2021; target history <= T-2; resident primary; registered sensitivity; pooled city-year MSE; macro-origin and per-origin stability
change: Reused frozen B1/B2/B3 predictions and reconstructed five compact target-history diagnostics; no new model or source
primary_result: Historical first-difference volatility passed the resident risk and decision-relevance gates; median abs Spearman 0.4281; high/remaining B3 MSE ratio 6.0006
stability_result: Resident risk gates passed across 11/11 positive directions; shrinkage comparator gain 6/11 and low-risk B3 advantage 5/11; registered did not materially reverse
interpretation: B3 risk is pre-identifiable, but risk identification alone does not establish repairability; volatility was the only activated next mechanism

hypothesis: Can deterministic robust local trend estimation repair B3 error in unstable history?
validation_contract: Same frozen contract; R1/R2 retained; no external data; no routing/blend/tuning; 40-city full coverage
change: Evaluated frozen B3/B4 and deterministic RLT3/RLT5 median-slope trends with raw/relative volatility and target-scale strata
primary_result: RLT3 resident pooled MSE 861.4909, about 1.256% below B3; RLT5 resident pooled MSE 933.8669; registered RLT5 256.7166
stability_result: RLT3 won 6/11 resident origins, raw high-volatility wins 6/11, normalized wins 7/11, non-high-scale volatile gain 0.1595%; RLT5 materially worsened registered
interpretation: The small RLT3 aggregate gain lacks the required cross-origin and scale-independent evidence; longer robust window is not a stable repair
